q: Which test must be done before a gynaecological laparoscopy?
why: Exclude pregnancy before any gynaecological procedure in women of childbearing age.

q: Why is an ETT usually used for laparoscopy?
o: Pneumoperitoneum and head-down raise airway pressure and aspiration risk
why: Higher airway pressures and head-down tilt make a tracheal tube the safer choice.

q: What should you check before waking a patient given atracurium in a short case?
why: Short cases risk residual block; check TOF and reverse if needed.

q: What is a cause of shoulder-tip pain after laparoscopy?
why: Residual CO₂ irritates the diaphragm, referring pain to the shoulder via C3–5.

q: When is a long-acting opioid such as oxycodone best given in a short laparoscopy?
why: Timing it towards the end gives analgesia in recovery without slowing emergence.
